info.title: ForgePilot orchestrator API
info.description: forgepilot-api/v1: the Node-to-UI contract of the ForgePilot pilot. The UI calls Node only, at an ephemeral loopback address; it never sees dsh sockets, boot tokens, Pi credentials, raw tool output, or provider credentials. Pi text is displayed only through the fail-closed pi_summary contract (DAT-191), whose classification boundary is DAT-192, whose trusted-source display boundary is DAT-193, and whose verifiable provenance record and read-side gate are DAT-194. Generated from the orchestrator implementation; shapes are defined by docs/contracts/forgepilot-api-v1.md.

get.summary: SSE stream of task events; replays by Last-Event-ID in sequence order from the durable projection, so a reconnect after an orchestrator restart resumes exactly where the client stopped without duplicating business events. A terminal task's stream always closes after its replay, including when Last-Event-ID is already anchored at task.terminal and the replay has nothing left to write.

parameters.description: Replay events after this event_id; unknown ids replay from the start.

association.description: Verifiable task/run/repository/revision binding. run_id and head_sha are projected from the authoritative dsh run; task_id, repository_id, and base_sha are the creation bindings dsh accepted and pinned for the run. Node never invents any of these values.

archived.description: Whether the cancelled task is in the archive view; the run status is unchanged.

pi_summary.description: Display-safe summary of the latest settled Pi turn for the current run (DAT-191). Null until a Pi session exists for the task. The raw pi.text_delta stream is never the display source: text is exposed only through this fail-closed, Node-judged summary, and only with a verifiable source record (DAT-194) — a summary whose source cannot be re-proven, including every legacy DAT-191/192 record, is served unavailable with text null.

governance.description: GitHub merge-boundary projection for the current head. Approvals and checks observed against an older head are invalidated: observations_valid turns false and merge_queue_eligible turns false until dsh observes them against the current head.

PiSummary.description: A display-safe natural-language summary of the latest settled Pi turn for one task run (DAT-191, classification boundary DAT-192, trust boundary DAT-193, verifiable provenance DAT-194). Displayability comes from provenance, not text inspection: text is exposed only when it comes from an auditable trusted source whose composition is reviewable in the orchestrator, and free model output never has one — no rule table can prove that arbitrary free text contains no command — so a settled model turn is withheld in full. The Node-side fail-closed classifier still names why material is kept out: credentials, shell syntax, absolute workspace paths, command invocations, argument material, unredacted logs, and opaque high-entropy strings fail closed as unsafe_content; an execution report or a sentence/line opener it cannot recognise as narrative prose (capitalisation confers no exemption; every line start is judged) fails closed as undecidable; a turn no rule flags is withheld as untrusted_source — a pass of the rule table is a classification, not a certification. Fail closed: an unavailable summary always carries text=null, never redacted or partial content. The one available path (DAT-193) is the turn's validated structured Pi report: closed-enum parameters on the report_turn_summary tool, server-side validation, and fixed wording composed by Node and framed as Pi's own report — never free model text, never run status or activity counts, and no additional model, network, or permission. A missing, unknown, or invalid report fails closed exactly like a turn with no report. Provenance (DAT-194): `source` is the machine-checkable record behind that claim — closed channel, proof-format version, task/run/turn attribution, and the echoed structured report — non-null exactly when status is available. The server re-proves every served available summary from it and withholds anything it cannot prove: a missing or unknown source, an unknown version, attribution to a different task/run/turn, tampered text, or a damaged record all serve as unavailable/untrusted_source with text null. Nothing is inferred from the text's shape, a timestamp, or the service's current version; no persisted record or recorded event is rewritten, so legacy DAT-191/192 free-text summaries keep their history but are never served as displayable. Lifecycle: null on the task until a Pi session exists; pending from session start (and at the start of every run) until a turn settles; then exactly one available/unavailable per settled turn, each replacing the previous summary — a turn settles (and publishes) exactly once, including the duplicated agent_error/agent_settled emission of a provider failure. A terminal task whose last turn never settled keeps status pending with text null; no summary is fabricated after the terminal frame. A pi.summary.updated event carries the same object on the SSE stream and in the timeline, replayable by Last-Event-ID like every other event, and passes the same provenance gate, so projection and events always agree.

run_id.description: The run whose Pi session produced this summary.

turn_id.description: The Pi turn this summary describes; null while pending.

text.description: The fixed-wording rendering of the turn's validated structured Pi report (DAT-193), framed as Pi's own report; non-null iff status is available. Never free model text. Bound to 240 characters.

unavailable_reason.description: Why no text is exposed: no_content (the settled turn produced no displayable text), unsafe_content (identified unsafe material), undecidable (the classifier could not recognise the turn: an execution report or an unrecognised sentence opener), gate_error (the classifier itself failed), untrusted_source (no rule flagged the content, but it has no auditable trusted source: free model text, a structured report that failed server-side validation, or a recorded summary whose source cannot be re-proven on read — legacy, missing, forged, or unknown-version provenance). Null unless status is unavailable. The enum is additive: clients render an unknown reason — and an unknown status — as a plain unavailable state. A legacy available summary is served this way after the DAT-194 gate downgrades it, so an old client that renders on status and text alone stops displaying historical free text without understanding the source field.

source.description: Verifiable provenance of `text`; non-null iff status is available. Null for pending and unavailable summaries, and for any summary whose source the server cannot re-proven (which is then served unavailable with text null instead of exposing an unproven source).

PiSummarySource.description: Verifiable provenance of a displayable summary's text (DAT-194). Non-null exactly when the summary is available. The trust chain it states: `kind` is the closed provenance channel (only `turn_report` — the model's closed-enum report_turn_summary tool, validated by the server and fixed-rendered by the server), `version` versions the proof format and rendering vocabulary (carried by the record; an unknown version is unverifiable), task_id/run_id/turn_id bind the proof to the task, run, and turn the summary describes, and `report` echoes the validated closed-enum report the text was rendered from. The server re-proves every served available summary from this record — valid report, re-rendered wording equal to the stored text, identical attribution, known kind and version — and serves anything it cannot prove as unavailable/untrusted_source with text null. Legacy DAT-191/192 summaries carry no source and are therefore never served as displayable. A client MAY corroborate these fields (enums, attribution, version); that check is not the safety boundary.

kind.description: The provenance channel. Closed set: any other kind is not a trusted source and fails closed.

version.description: Version of the source proof format and its rendering vocabulary. This contract defines 1; a client MUST treat an unknown version as unverifiable, and the server serves such summaries as unavailable.

task_id.description: Task the proof is bound to.

run_id.description: Run the proof is bound to; must equal the summary's run_id.

turn_id.description: Pi turn the proof is bound to; must equal the summary's turn_id.

TurnReport.description: One validated structured Pi turn report: the closed-enum parameters of the report_turn_summary tool (DAT-193). Every parameter is a key from a closed vocabulary — there is no free-text field — and the server validates membership and cardinality before recording it. Summary text is fixed-rendered from exactly this structure.

bearerAuth.description: Per-process API bearer token, minted at orchestrator start and written 0600 to the API token file. The UI reads that file and sends it as Authorization: Bearer <token> on every request; possession of the token authorizes acting as the local operator, approvals included.
